newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares on hold before U.S. Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: German shares on hold before U.S. Fed meeting.

text.p: German shares traded flat in early Monday dealings and were expected to remain within narrow ranges ahead of any U.S. interest rate indications emerging from Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares was barely one point higher at 3,036.21 in early bourse trade, with the IBIS-DAX index of electronic trade 2.00 lower at 3,036.10.
"The Bund (debt) market had already by last week factored in the impact of a small rise in interest rates. We think the outlook from this meeting will be neutral now," one trader said.
March DAX futures slipped four points to 3,045.0.
Shares in German diversified utilities Veba AG and RWE AG fell heavily following a British newspaper report that Cable & Wireless Plc was planning to exit its telecom alliance with them.
The Times earlier on Monday reported that the British group was looking to abandon its alliance with the two. Veba fell 1.75 marks to 88.85, while RWE slipped 1.40 marks to 67.90.
Dealers said the report had prompted some profit-taking in the German utility sector that had recently been setting in after a strong bull run in the sector.

Builders Hochtief and Holzmann both rose on a report, later denied by both, that Hochtief planned to "pool" its 20 percent stake with a shareholding owned by Deutsche Bank in a bid to increase its control on Holzmann.
Hochtief was 30 pfennigs up at 67.0 marks, Holzmann two marks higher at 420.0.
Dealers said other significant stock movements were largely related to the continued strength of the dollar, which traded around 1.6420 marks.
Software group SAP continued its rise after last week's strong 1996 figures, rising 1.50 marks to 244.0.
